method: R1 blind suread (subagent read text only, no md/rules)

facts.fact: After coffee she checks the driveway to make sure Eeling hasn’t arrived yet (wishing he’d drive off the road into a tree) and decides she has time for a final phone call.
facts.anchor: She checks the driveway to make sure Eeling hasn’t arrived yet

facts.fact: She takes the old iPhone back out of the drawer, holding the belief that the calls and her voice are the only things keeping Tommy from succumbing to the darkness.
facts.anchor: It’s the belief that the only thing keeping Tommy from succumbing to the darkness inside him are the calls and her voice.

facts.fact: She notes Paige McMahon’s murder was five years ago and there has not been another killing since.
facts.anchor: Paige McMahon’s murder was five years ago. There hasn’t been another killing since.

facts.fact: She reasserts her pledge: if the police can’t keep Tommy from killing, she will do her best to.
facts.anchor: If the police can’t keep him from killing, she’ll do her best to.

facts.fact: She calls Colm Tyring, who answers breathlessly, as if he rushed to the phone, asking if she is okay.
facts.anchor: Colm Tyring says a little breathlessly as if he’s rushed to the phone.

facts.fact: Colm says he stayed over at the school because there was a midnight class observing the Orionids meteor shower for extra credit.
facts.anchor: There was a midnight class observing the Orionids meteor shower. Extra credit.

facts.fact: Colm says Eeling came bearing threats: if Colm didn’t tell him what he wanted, Eeling would reveal D’s and Leah’s identities and ruin everything they built.
facts.anchor: Came bearing threats. If I didn’t tell him what he wanted he was going to reveal D’s and Leah’s identities, ruin everything they’d built.

facts.fact: Colm recounts that Eeling asked what Tommy was like growing up, whether he showed strange behaviors, tortured animals, and how finding out affected Colm and his life.
facts.anchor: What Tommy was like growing up, did I notice any strange behaviors from him, did he torture animals, that type of thing.

facts.fact: Colm relays that Tommy said Hattie told him she couldn’t forgive what he’d done but could accept it, and asks what she meant; she answers that children are your responsibility no matter how old they get.
facts.anchor: you told him you couldn’t forgive what he’d done, but you could accept it. What did you mean?
